name: Union Gap
tax_rate: 4% lodging tax plus a Tourism Promotion Area charge; DOR 2024 distributions were $151,421 state-shared, $150,919 special and $245,890 TPA
deadline_pattern: Application released about August 1 and due in mid-August for the following calendar year (Aug 15, 2025 for 2026 funds; Aug 17, 2026 for 2027 funds); late or incomplete applications are not considered
typical_open: Early August (application released August 1, 2026; notice dated July 30, 2026)
annual_pool: Not published; the application and public notice state no total pool or award cap
contact: Teresa Lopez, Deputy City Clerk, teresa.lopez@uniongapwa.gov, (509) 248-0432 (application form) / 509-249-9202 (LTAC meeting notice); mail to City of Union Gap, Attn: LTAC Committee, PO Box 3008, Union Gap, WA 98903 or 102 West Ahtanum Road
notes: Union Gap runs a simple annual LTAC budget-request cycle: a one-page notice and application go up around August 1 and are due in mid-August for the next calendar year, submitted by email or mail to the Deputy City Clerk. The LTAC forecasts revenue, covers city operating costs and debt service first, then recommends funding to City Council, which may accept or deny. The form gives preference to projects operating or improving city-owned facilities that generate overnight stays and to year-round promotion through the destination marketing organization; the LTAC also interviewed candidates for a Tourism Promoter Coordinator position in June 2026. Funding is one year, reimbursement only, with no advance payments.

name: Langley
tax_rate: 4% total (2% basic plus 2% special per DOR Q2 2026 table; mayor's February 2026 memo cites 4% on hotels, motels, Airbnbs, RV parks)
deadline_pattern: Applications are reviewed in late summer and awards approved by City Council in October or November for the following year (council approved 2024 awards Nov 2023 and 2026 awards Oct 6, 2025); the mayor said Langley's allocation runs after Island County's and the program would be reviewed in the first quarter of 2026, so the 2027 cycle timing may change
typical_open: Summer (exact dates not published; 2026 awards approved October 6, 2025)
annual_pool: $56,816 awarded for 2026 across 11 recipients (requests totaled $116,075); $98,100 awarded for 2024 from about $122,000 anticipated. A February 2026 proposal would dedicate 25% of current-year collections to the grant cycle and 25% to the Chamber visitor center contract
contact: City of Langley, Mayor Kennedy Horstman (langleywa.org; the city website could not be fetched for this entry, so no staff contact was confirmed)
notes: Langley disbanded its standing Lodging Tax Advisory Commission and now uses a temporary ad hoc committee (two lodging-tax collectors and two recipients) that scores applications on countywide benefit, shoulder-season focus, economic impact and regenerative tourism, then recommends awards to council. The 2026 round spread $56,816 across 11 applicants as supplemental 'seed money' with no one fully funded. In February 2026 the mayor proposed reallocating lodging tax so that 12.5% goes to Island County joint tourism, 31.25% to city tourism facilities, 6.25% to affordable housing, and the remaining 50% split evenly between the grant cycle and the Chamber visitor center contract; the council also planned to review the whole program in early 2026 with three new councilmembers. A follow-up search for an official langleywa.org program page or application form returned nothing; apply through City Hall.

deadline_pattern: Application window runs September 1 through September 30 for the following year (Sept 1-30, 2024 for 2025 funds); applicants present to the commissioners in early November and award resolutions are adopted in January

The 2025 round gave $209,000 to four established recipients, with the regional DMO Visit Lewis Clark Valley taking $90,000, so little is left for new events unless revenue grows. The county site served only the application-window text, and the September 15, 2025 agenda PDF was unreadable, so the 2026-cycle amounts, eligibility language and staff contact are unconfirmed.

name: Coupeville
tax_rate: 4% total (2% basic plus 2% special per DOR Q2 2026 table); the town calls its program the '2 percent' lodging tax grant
deadline_pattern: Applications due to the Clerk-Treasurer at Town Hall by the last business day of September; scored applications discussed at the first council meeting in October and awards made by the second October meeting (policy adopted 2017, amended 2018)
typical_open: Late summer; forms available from Town Hall ahead of the end-of-September deadline
annual_pool: Roughly $25,000 to $50,000 a year depending on carryover: $33,250 awarded for 2019, $39,300 for 2022 (about $50,000 available), $49,000 for 2023 (drawing on about $64,000 accumulated during the pandemic)
contact: Town of Coupeville Clerk-Treasurer, Town Hall, 4 NE Seventh Street, Coupeville (townofcoupeville.org; site could not be fetched, so current clerk name, email and phone are unconfirmed; Kelly Beech was Clerk-Treasurer in 2017)
notes: Coupeville is under 5,000 population so it has no statutory LTAC; the Town Council itself scores the applications using set criteria and makes the awards at its October meetings. Since 2017 any nonprofit may apply (the council replaced a fixed recipient list), with preference for activities inside town limits, shoulder-season (October to May) events, direct economic benefit and overnight stays, and projects that highlight local history, natural resources or traditions. The Chamber of Commerce visitor center ($20,000 to $26,000 a year), Musselfest marketing, the Island County Historical Museum and Tour de Whidbey are regular recipients and the town keeps a share for its own tourism activities.

presentation.pattern: No formal presentation; council discusses each written application at its first October meeting and applicants may attend

meeting_schedule: No committee; Town Council handles 2% grants at its two regular October meetings each year
pool_note: DOR Table L1 2024 local lodging tax distributions: $88,572. Most recent published round (2023 funds, approved fall 2022): $49,000 awarded to four applicants, all at or above their request (Chamber $26,000 visitor center, Island County Historical Museum $10,000, CHWA Musselfest $8,000, WhidbeyHealth Foundation Tour de Whidbey $5,000), funded from about $30,000 in 2021 collections plus roughly $64,000 accumulated during the pandemic; the town retained the balance for its own tourism uses. tax_rate: 2% basic on all lodging; additional 2% special applies only to properties with 40 or more units (DOR Q2 2026 table); 2018 budget estimated lodging tax revenue at $190,500
deadline_pattern: Main allocation is adopted by council resolution in February for the calendar year (Resolution F-470 on Feb 10, 2026); historically the committee also took applications twice a year with a late-February deadline, and it has approved individual requests by separate resolution during the year (March 2025, April 2026, November 2024)

notes: Cheney's LTAC, chaired by Councilwoman Danielle LaBar, reviews written requests and recommends them to City Council, which adopts each disbursement by resolution; the 2026 round totaled $49,097 with Mayfest as the largest recipient, and smaller requests such as the Cheney Merchants Association's Holiday Hoopla ($10,900 for December 2024) and the Cheney Depot Society ($13,894 in April 2026) are handled as they come. name: Electric City
tax_rate: 4% total (2% basic plus 2% special per DOR Q2 2026 table)
deadline_pattern: Recent cycle: applications accepted April 15 to April 30 (due 5 p.m. April 30, 2024) for that year's events; earlier cycles took requests in September for the following year with council action in October. Confirm the current window with City Hall
annual_pool: Not published; 2024 lodging tax distributions were $58,217 (DOR), revenue ran $74,000 to $107,400 a year in 2018-2020, and past award packages were $40,000 (2018) and $50,500 to outside groups plus $288,050 to the city's Ice Age Park (2019)
contact: Peggy Nevsimal, City of Electric City, PO Box 130, Electric City, WA 99123 (applications addressed to her per the 2024 form; title, phone and email not stated)
notes: Electric City has a written Lodging Tax Fund application (2024 General Information and Event Promotion Application) open only to public and nonprofit agencies, with the original plus three copies due at City Hall and disbursement after a post-event report; its council Lodging Tax Committee reviews requests and recommends to the full council. Priority goes to projects likely to generate overnight stays, promote the city to visitors from outside Grant County, involve partnerships or improve city-owned tourism facilities, and recipients must mention Electric City lodging in advertising. Regular recipients are the Grand Coulee Dam Area Chamber (Colorama, fireworks), Ridge Riders rodeo events, Port District 7's Banks Lake Golf Course, Coulee Area Park and Recreation District and the Pioneer Museum, while the city has reserved large sums for its own Ice Age Park and trail projects.

presentation.pattern: No presentation requirement in the application; council has heard requests from applicants at regular meetings in past years

meeting_schedule: Council Lodging Tax Committee reviews applications after the window closes and brings recommendations to a regular council meeting (first and second Tuesdays)
pool_note: DOR Table L1 2024 local lodging tax distributions: $58,217. No current-year pool is published; in 2019 the council approved $338,550 of accumulated funds, of which $288,050 went to the city's own Ice Age Park and promotion and $50,500 to five outside groups (Chamber $20,000, Ridge Riders $20,000, CAPRD $7,000, Run the Dam $3,000, Pioneer Museum $500).
